summary.text: Least squares is a method for finding the best-fit model by minimizing the sum of the squared residuals, the differences between observed values and the values the model predicts.
The linear problem has a closed-form solution, while the nonlinear problem is usually solved by iterative refinement, approximating the system by a linear one at each step.
Legendre published the first clear exposition in 1805, and Gauss went further by connecting the method with probability and the normal distribution.

facts.label: Gauss's claim
facts.value: He said he had held the method since 1795

facts.label: Finding Ceres
facts.value: Gauss's least-squares predictions let astronomers relocate the asteroid

facts.label: Residual
facts.value: Observed value minus the value the model predicts

facts.label: Fast adoption
facts.value: Standard in French, Italian and Prussian astronomy within ten years

items.prompt: A line predicts 10 for a data point whose observed value is 13. How does least squares treat that gap of 3?

options.label: It adds 3 to the gaps from other points, unsquared, and minimizes that total
It ignores any gap smaller than 5
It squares the gap, adds it to the other squared gaps, and picks the model with the smallest total
It keeps only the single largest gap

items.explain: The method determines the best-fit model by minimizing the sum of the squared residuals, the differences between observed and predicted values.

items.prompt: An asteroid was tracked for only 40 days before vanishing in the Sun's glare, and astronomers needed to find it again. Whose predictions succeeded?

options.label: Those from Gauss using least-squares analysis
Those solving Kepler's nonlinear equations directly
Those averaging the 40 positions
Those from Laplace using absolute deviations

items.explain: The only predictions that let von Zach relocate Ceres were those made by the young Gauss with least-squares analysis, without solving Kepler's complicated nonlinear equations.

items.prompt: You are fitting a curve to a set of measurements. What does least squares actually adjust to get the best fit?

options.label: The measurements themselves, nudged toward the curve
The number of data points used
Only the largest residual
The parameters of the model function

items.explain: The objective consists of adjusting the parameters of a model function to best fit a data set.

items.prompt: A fitting problem is nonlinear in its unknowns. How is it usually solved?

options.label: By repeated refinement, approximating by a linear system at each step
By a closed-form formula, exactly as in the linear case
It cannot be solved by least squares
By dropping the nonlinear terms permanently

items.explain: Linear least squares has a closed-form solution, but the nonlinear problem is usually solved by iterative refinement, approximating the system by a linear one each time.

items.prompt: Legendre and Gauss both claimed the method. What did Gauss add that went beyond Legendre?

options.label: The first use of the method in astronomy
A link between the method, probability and the normal distribution
A switch from squared errors to absolute errors
A formula for fitting only straight lines

items.explain: After a priority dispute with Legendre, Gauss is credited with connecting the method of least squares with the principles of probability and the normal distribution.

items.prompt: Laplace modelled errors with a two-sided exponential distribution and used the sum of absolute deviations, hoping to get the arithmetic mean as the best estimate. What did his estimator turn out to be?

options.label: The arithmetic mean after all
The largest observation
The posterior median
The sum of squared residuals

items.explain: He had hoped to obtain the arithmetic mean, but his estimator was instead the posterior median.
